name: shell
what: The shell tokenizer keeps quoted text from looking like a command, reads the commands inside a double-quoted command substitution as commands of their own, and never mistakes an output redirection for an argument.

faults.fault: The target of an output redirection stays as a word, so > out.txt reads as an argument.
The file descriptor stays as a word, so 2>&1 leaves a stray 2 among the arguments.
The ampersand in 2>&1 ends the command, so a stray 1 reads as a command of its own.
The ampersand in &> ends the command, so the words after the redirection become a new command.
A dangling redirection swallows the first word of the next command, so git status loses its name.
A command substitution inside double quotes is no longer scanned, so the quote ends at the first inner double quote and a heredoc body line becomes a command.
faults.find: if (src[i] === '$' && src[i + 1] === '(') i = scan(src, i + 2, true, commands);
faults.replace: if (false) i = scan(src, i + 2, true, commands);

faults.fault: Backticks inside double quotes are read as plain text, so a command inside them goes unseen.
A closing parenthesis ends the substitution even when it closes a nested group, so the rest of the quoted text is misread.
withoutInput keeps the file named after a separate <, so that file still reads as an argument.
